metaDescription: Six rolling and tabletop dust collectors compared on airflow, bag size, filtration and weight, for garages where the machine must move to the work.
expertTake: The BUCKTOOL 1.5 HP is the pick for a garage that needs planer-grade airflow on casters, and the POWERTEC 560 CFM unit is the value choice for a saw and a drill press. The PSI tabletop unit is a specialist for carving and sanding, not a chip mover. Anyone who needs to collect chips from several machines at once should buy something fixed with ducting instead.
introParagraphs: A mobile shop usually means a garage shared with a car or a bench carried out of a closet. In that setting the best collector is the one that actually gets rolled to the machine, because a heavy unit parked in the corner with a long hose never gets used.

Mobility trades against capacity. A machine small enough to lift moves less air and holds less waste, and that makes bag size, filter grade and wheel quality more important than headline motor numbers. Read the details before trusting a single rating.

products.name: BUCKTOOL 1.5 HP 6-Inch Inlet Dust Collector, 1100-1654 CFM
products.description:
The BUCKTOOL stands out by pairing a fan-cooled, dual-voltage induction motor with a 6 inch main inlet and an internal dust baffle. The baffle lets heavy chips drop before the air reaches the filter, which keeps the bag from loading as fast as a bag collector with no separation. Six inches is the right inlet for a planer or jointer, a size most portable units never reach.

The range of 1100 to 1654 CFM is a wide spread, and the lower number is the one to plan around. Filtration is stated as 98 percent at 5 microns, which is better than a bare 5 micron bag but not in the class of a HEPA filter, so fine dust still deserves a respirator. Next to the POWERTEC 800 CFM unit it moves more air and also takes more floor.

Ownership centers on weight and the filter. This is the heaviest rolling machine here, so wheel quality and a flat floor matter. Clean the filter on a schedule, because a clogged filter makes an induction motor work harder, and empty the collection bag before it passes the halfway mark. If your garage floor is sloped or uneven, secure the machine so it does not creep on its casters.
products.bestFor: A garage shop that needs planer-capable airflow without a fixed cyclone.
pros: 6 inch inlet suits planers and jointers
Induction motor runs cooler than brushed rivals
Internal baffle drops chips before the filter
Dual voltage allows 120 or 240 volt wiring
cons: Heaviest unit and a large footprint for a mobile model
Filtration is not HEPA grade, so fine dust needs a respirator

products.name: POWERTEC 1 HP 560 CFM Portable Dust Collector, 1 Micron Bag
products.description:
The POWERTEC 560 CFM is a compact caster-mounted machine whose standout feature is a reusable 1 micron bag with a window to show dust level and a zipper for emptying. A finer bag keeps more of the harmful dust out of your breathing air, and the window removes the guesswork about when to empty.

It is a one-tool machine. At 560 CFM it handles a table saw, router table or drill press well, but it will lag on a planer or with a long hose. A fine bag loads quickly as well, so suction falls faster than with a coarser rival unless you shake the bag regularly. Against the same brand's 800 CFM model it gives up airflow and costs less.

The zipper emptying is the part to respect. Dust comes out in a cloud if you open it carelessly, so empty it outdoors and wear a mask. Check the clamp where the upper bag meets the housing every few weeks, since leaks hide there. Casters are small, so a smooth floor helps.
products.bestFor: A hobbyist who uses a table saw or router table and wants a fine bag at a modest cost.
pros: 1 micron bag filters finer than most in the class
Window shows the dust level at a glance
Compact body fits beside a bench
Zipper bag is reusable and easy to empty
cons: 560 CFM is thin for a planer
Fine bag loads quickly and needs regular shaking

products.name: SHOPMAX 20-Gallon 6.3-Amp Dust Collector, 12 in. Impeller
products.description:
The SHOPMAX uses a 12 inch impeller, the largest wheel among the smaller machines, to push a maximum of 677 CFM from a 6.3-amp motor. A large wheel spinning at moderate speed is the efficient route to airflow, and it usually means less screaming noise than a small impeller doing the same work.

The 20 gallon bag gives it breathing room that the smaller handle-carry units lack, so a saw session does not end with a full bag. It is still a bag collector, which means fine dust passes into the room unless you use a finer filter. The maximum airflow figure is a ceiling with the inlet open, so a hose will cut it substantially.

Because the housing is bigger than a compact collector, it behaves more like a small shop unit than a carry-around. Keep an eye on the bag seams and empty before it fills. Roll it by the handle on a level floor, and park it where the cord does not cross a walkway.
products.bestFor: A shop that wants a larger bag and a big impeller without stepping to a 1.5 HP machine.
pros: 12 inch impeller moves air efficiently
20 gallon bag is roomy for the class
6.3-amp motor draws modest current
Moves easily from tool to tool
cons: 677 CFM figure is a ceiling not a delivered number
Bag filtration needs upgrading for fine dust

products.name: PSI Woodworking DC725 Tabletop Dust Collector, 725 CFM
products.description:
This is a different kind of portable machine: a 24 pound tabletop unit that draws dust through three quiet fans into an adjustable hood. It targets carving, sanding, grinding and woodburning, where dust rises from a small bench area rather than being thrown by a spinning blade into a port.

The airflow figure of 725 CFM looks large, but this is an open-air capture device rather than a ducted collector, so it cannot pull chips from a saw or a planer. It does not attach to a tool port and has no chip bag to speak of. What it does well is catch the fine floating dust at the bench and clean the air without a hose.

Because the fans are computer-grade, there are no brushes and little to maintain beyond the filter media and the hood. Keep it on a stable bench so vibration does not walk it, and wipe the hood regularly. Buy it as a companion to a bag collector, not as a replacement.
products.bestFor: Carvers and sanders working at a bench where airborne fine dust is the problem.
pros: 24 pounds lifts onto any bench
Variable speed keeps noise down
Quiet fans have no brushes to wear
Footprint of 23 by 8 inches fits small benches
cons: Cannot connect to a saw or planer port
Captures floating dust only, not chips

products.name: WEN DC3401 5.7-Amp Dust Collector, 12-Gallon Bag, Handle
products.description:
The WEN DC3401 is small enough to lift by an onboard handle, and it rides a mobile base or hangs on a wall. A 5.7-amp brushed motor spins a 6 inch impeller to a 660 CFM rating, and a 4 inch port connects to most bench tools.

Its price is the lowest in the group in most listings and its weight makes it the easiest to carry between a garage and a driveway. The 12 gallon bag fills sooner than the SHOPMAX 20 gallon bag, and the brushed motor is noisier than an induction model like the BUCKTOOL. It suits saws and sanders but not a planer.

Store it upright and keep the hose coiled loosely. Brushes will need replacing eventually, and the small bag is the first thing to wear. It is the machine to buy if you are unsure how much collecting you will actually do.
products.bestFor: A first-time buyer or a tight garage where the unit has to be carried and stored.
pros: Carry handle makes it the easiest to move
Low entry cost for a branded unit
Wall mount option for storage
4 inch port fits common bench tools
cons: 12 gallon bag fills quickly with a planer

products.name: POWERTEC 1 HP 800 CFM Dust Collector, Mobile Base, 1 Micron
products.description:
The 800 CFM POWERTEC sits between the 560 CFM model and the BUCKTOOL. It puts a 1 HP motor behind a 1 micron upper bag and rolls on a sturdy caster base about 15 by 25 inches, so it is a step up in airflow with the same fine filtration.

It still uses a standard bag layout, so it loads faster than the baffled BUCKTOOL and will struggle with a planer fed full-width boards. The 800 CFM rating suits a table saw plus a long run to a miter station. Against the 560 CFM sibling it moves roughly forty percent more air for a modest step in size.

Shake the upper bag often and check the clamp rings for leaks. Casters need a flat floor, and the cord should be kept short since the motor draws real current. It makes a sensible choice when the 560 CFM unit feels thin but the BUCKTOOL feels excessive.
products.bestFor: A garage with a table saw and a miter station that wants more airflow without a large machine.
pros: 800 CFM exceeds most compact rivals
1 micron bag keeps fine dust out of the air
Caster base rolls easily
Includes both upper and lower bags

buyingCriteria.explanation: A portable collector is only useful if you will actually move it, and wheels decide that. Small casters stall on cracks and cords, so a heavy unit like the BUCKTOOL wants a flat, clean floor. The handle-carry WEN DC3401 and the 24 pound PSI DC725 trade capacity for lightness. Weigh how often you will lift the unit up a step or into a trunk before choosing.

Rated CFM is an open-inlet figure. Once a 4 inch hose and a blast gate are attached, a machine rated at 560 CFM like the POWERTEC may deliver barely enough for a router table. Short hoses preserve airflow, which is the main benefit of a rolling machine. A 6 inch inlet, such as on the BUCKTOOL, is the only portable route to planer-grade airflow.

Portable machines have small bags, and a thickness planer will fill a 12 gallon bag in a few boards. The SHOPMAX holds 20 gallons, the WEN DC3401 only 12, and the BUCKTOOL uses a baffle to drop chips so the filter stays clearer. Match bag size to chip volume. Emptying a full bag mid-job costs more time than the extra gallons of capacity.

A 1 micron bag like the POWERTEC protects lungs more than a coarse bag, but it clogs sooner. The BUCKTOOL filter is quoted at 98 percent of 5 micron particles, a middle ground. Fine bags demand regular shaking, otherwise suction collapses. If you mostly saw, take the finer bag; if you plane, take the baffle design.

Induction motors, as in the BUCKTOOL, run cooler and quieter, while brushed motors such as in the WEN DC3401 are louder and need new brushes. In a garage with neighbours, motor noise limits when you can work. A big, slow impeller like the SHOPMAX 12 inch also helps lower the pitch.

A tabletop unit like the PSI DC725 does not connect to a tool and cannot capture chips. It cleans floating fine dust, which makes it a partner to a collector rather than a substitute. Buyers sometimes assume that a high CFM figure means the machine can collect at the source, and with an open-air unit it cannot.

specDecoder.meaning: The size of the port where the hose attaches. Wider inlets pass more air with less friction.
specDecoder.watchFor: The BUCKTOOL has a 6 inch main inlet while the others use 4 inch ports.

specDecoder.meaning: Some makers quote a range, with the low end closer to realistic use.
specDecoder.watchFor: The BUCKTOOL quotes 1100 to 1654 CFM, so plan around the lower number.

specDecoder.meaning: The size of the fan wheel. Larger wheels move more air at a lower, quieter speed.
specDecoder.watchFor: The SHOPMAX 12 inch impeller is the largest among the small units.

specDecoder.meaning: The smallest particle the filter is rated to catch. Smaller numbers filter more and load faster.
specDecoder.watchFor: The POWERTEC uses 1 micron bags, the BUCKTOOL a 2 micron filter.

specDecoder.meaning: How much you must lift to store or transport the machine.
specDecoder.watchFor: The PSI DC725 weighs 24 pounds, far less than any of the bag collectors.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability in practice
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered weight, wheel type and handles against how often the machine has to move. A unit that is never moved is not portable. The WEN DC3401 and PSI DC725 scored highest for carrying.

howWeEvaluated.title: Airflow per footprint
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rated CFM against the size of each machine and the inlet size. The BUCKTOOL leads the field with a 6 inch inlet and a 1100 to 1654 CFM range, while the POWERTEC 560 CFM sits at the other end.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration and loading
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed micron rating against how fast each filter clogs. A 1 micron bag is best for air quality but needs frequent cleaning. A baffle that drops chips earns credit because it prolongs filter life.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and motor design
howWeEvaluated.description: Induction motors and large slow impellers rank above small brushed units. The WEN DC3401 brushed motor ranks lowest for noise, and the PSI DC725 quiet fans rank highest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Chip capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared bag volume to the chip output of typical tools. The SHOPMAX 20 gallon bag and the BUCKTOOL baffle lead, while a 12 gallon bag suits only light use.

cards.label: Rolling collector
cards.text: A rolling unit like the BUCKTOOL or POWERTEC connects to a tool port and captures chips and dust at the source. It is the right answer for saws, planers and sanders with a dust port.

cards.label: Tabletop cleaner
cards.text: The PSI DC725 draws fine dust from a bench through fans and a hood. It is quiet and light but cannot connect to a tool, so chips stay behind.

howToChoose.note: Collect at the source with a rolling unit first; add the tabletop cleaner only if fine dust still floats.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a unit you can roll with one hand, an inlet that matches your heaviest tool, and a bag you can empty outdoors. Garage floors are rough, so avoid tiny casters on a heavy machine.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The POWERTEC 800 CFM fits the typical garage with a saw and a router table. Step up to the BUCKTOOL if a planer joins the shop.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you plane lumber or run long sessions. The BUCKTOOL buys a 6 inch inlet and an induction motor, which no cheaper unit here can match.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you cut a few boards a month. The WEN DC3401 or POWERTEC 560 CFM clears bench saw chips and costs far less.

maintenance.why: A bag past halfway loses suction quickly. Empty outdoors and wear a respirator.
Fine bags pack with dust and cut airflow. The 1 micron bags need it most.
Sawdust jams casters and makes a heavy unit hard to move. Clear them and check the swivels.
Loose clamps leak, and cracked hose loses airflow. Replace a split hose at once.
The WEN DC3401 motor uses brushes that wear out. Replace them when you see sparking.

faq.q: What makes a dust collector portable?
faq.a: A portable unit is light enough to roll or lift to the tool, usually on casters or with a handle. It trades capacity for mobility, so bags are smaller and airflow lower than on a fixed cyclone.

faq.q: Can a portable unit run a thickness planer?
faq.a: Only if it has a large inlet and a big bag. The BUCKTOOL 1.5 HP with a 6 inch inlet is the one here that suits a planer. Smaller units will clog quickly.

faq.q: How much does a portable unit cost to run?
faq.a: Running cost is mostly electricity and bags. Brushed motors need new brushes occasionally and bags wear at the seams. There is no oil or fuel.

faq.q: Does higher CFM always mean better collection?
faq.a: No, because CFM is measured with the inlet open. Hose length, bends and filter loading cut it. A machine with a larger impeller and a short hose often beats a higher rated unit.

faq.q: Do I still need a respirator?
faq.a: Yes. Even a 1 micron bag lets some fine dust escape during emptying, and the finest particles are the harmful ones. Wear a mask when you empty the bag.

faq.q: Is a tabletop cleaner enough on its own?
faq.a: Not for chips. The PSI DC725 handles floating dust but does not connect to tools. Use it as a companion to a collector.
